evidence: M-O s.v. hockey: ice hockey (Helfer: alsulegia glaciālis)
terms.comment: Morgan–Owens traces the word to Mercuriale (1569), who quotes it from a Latin Avicenna as the Arabic name of the crooked sticks of polo, virgīs retortīs dictīs alsulegiam; Helfer made a Latin noun of it, and Traupman and Andresian follow. Vowel lengths as Traupman marks them.

terms.gloss: hockey, on ice or on grass
terms.comment: Traupman’s first word for ice hockey, and his only one for field hockey; “play hockey” is hoccejō lūdere.
Morgan–Owens’s choice, from zucanium (Byzantine τζυκάνιον), polo.

sources: Lewis & Short: alsius · Lewis & Short: glacialis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 48, checked against the searchable text of the book on 11 November 2026.
